findings.summary: The criterion 5 demonstration can pass without checking anything: M19 never scans an untracked docs/spec.toml.
findings.evidence: `athena_files()` builds its list from `git ls-files -z`, so new untracked files are skipped. The producer must not change git state, so docs/spec.toml will be untracked when the verifier runs `cargo test -p xtask`. The plan admits this ('If the file is only untracked, the verifier checks the same text with `git diff` once it is staged'), which means the demonstration's 'fails without the behavior' claim is false in the environment that will actually run it. Fix: In xtask/tests/spec.rs, add a test that reads docs/spec.toml directly and checks it against `athena_context::briefs::boundary_words()` and `boundary_fragments()`. These are public at crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs lines 238 and 263, and athena-context is already a dev-dependency. Use the same matching as policy.rs: whole words, case-insensitive, built with `regex`. Add a negative case that plants a banned word in an in-memory copy and expects it to be flagged. Name this test in the enforcement.md row. Keep policy.rs unchanged.
findings.location: Plan › Demonstrations › Criterion 5; xtask/tests/policy.rs lines 53–81 and 165–184

findings.summary: The Olympus-only restriction may still pass quotes from the relayed Athena-brief text, and the 2A item is owner-side.
findings.evidence: BRIEF.md line 1007 (2A) is about who runs Athena and uses a banned word. Lines 1021–1024 ('The operator is the brain for now') are owner-side. Both come after '# Project Olympus', so the position check does not exclude them, and the out-of-scope list excludes such statements. Fix: Say plainly that 2A and the 'brain' addendum are out of scope and get no requirement. Do not try to quote around them, because criterion 5 forbids statements about who runs Athena. Record that exclusion in D111 or in a header comment in the spec.
findings.location: Plan › Decisions 2 and Risks (2A and 'brain' addenda)

findings.summary: The negative tests should assert the specific reason, not just that some problem was reported.
findings.evidence: `check` returns Vec<String>. If a negative test only asserts the list is non-empty, it could pass for an unrelated reason, such as a mutation that breaks another field. Fix: Have each negative test assert that a problem string names the cause and id it planted, such as 'duplicate id OLY-001' or 'supersedes OLY-999 not found'. Also assert that the unmutated spec yields no problems in the same test.

findings.summary: The open-question candidate on the API surface depends on text outside the Olympus layer.
findings.evidence: The plan suggests pairing 'I'm not sold the API surface should be considered settled' (BRIEF.md line 1019) with 'earlier parts of the Athena brief', but the checker restricts quotes to text after '# Project Olympus'. Fix: Choose a pair with both quotes after line 550. One example is 'reconsider its own design every few jobs' (line 1017) against a stable-design or governed self-modification line in R5. Another is 5A's 'No formal ontology for now' (line 1011).

summary: The plan fits the request and the accepted reading. I checked its claims in the snapshot. `toml`, `serde`, `regex` and `athena-context` are already dev-dependencies of xtask (xtask/Cargo.toml lines 20–24). D110 is the last decision, so D111 is the right next number. The BRIEF.md headings the coverage keys rely on all exist ('## 10. Final system acceptance', '### R1 — …' through R8, '### Phase 1 — …' through Phase 6 with their 'Acceptance:' lines, '### 2026-10-17: Olympus' with items 3C, 4A, 5A and 7A). The ontology checker accepts sources written as 'D111'. The plan also identifies the M19 word list correctly (policy.rs lines 88–131). One gap matters. The criterion 5 demonstration relies on policy.rs's `athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where`, which scans only `git ls-files` output. The producer cannot change git state, so a new, untracked docs/spec.toml would not be scanned when the verifier runs, and the test would pass even if the spec contained a banned word. The plan admits this in its open questions but does not close it. The rest are minor tightenings.
